input.quote: 14.2.2 At-Will Termination by PB. PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
input.rationale: PB's only at-will exit (14.2.2) is not an exercisable convenience right: it is unavailable until SFJ has funded $60 million of Development Costs, it closes on receipt of the first Regulatory Approval, and the notice period is redacted. Across a Term that runs until the last Approval Payment (14.1), PB therefore has no convenience termination at either the preferred (30 days) or the fallback (60-90 days) standard, which is a material failure of the fallback. Operative cure at the preferred level: 14.2.2 now reads "PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ, in which case SFJ will refund to PB, pro rata, any amounts prepaid by PB for the period after the effective date of termination", and new 14.2.11 bars SFJ from terminating for convenience during the Term. SFJ's exits at 14.2.3 (Material Adverse Event), 14.2.6 (Change of Control) and 14.2.10 (JSC deadlock) are event-triggered rather than convenience rights, so they and their payment formulas are retained without contradiction and no cross-reference (including Section 5.2.2.2's reference to 14.2.10) is left dangling. The retained 300% Development Cost payment is a fallback-level fee-cap point, so it is offered commercially in the comment rather than redlined at the preferred level.

proposal.summary: PB may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts; SFJ has no convenience termination right during the Term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the $60 million funding and pre-approval gates so PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice, with a pro-rata refund of any prepaid amounts, and we added an express bar on SFJ terminating for convenience during the Term. If preferred, we can move to our fallback of 60-90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

ops.text: No Termination for Convenience by SFJ. SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
